summary: Platform tower on Mount Seneca, Cattaraugus County, NY, listed by FFLA as gone; the summit sits 2,106 ft high and a park trail runs to it.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the Mount Seneca platform as gone. No source read dates its build or removal.

visit.trail_note: The Allegany State Park article lists a 4.0-mile Bear Caves trail to Mt. Seneca.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only source for the platform itself is the FFLA county line (Platform Tower Gone, Cattaraugus County, 42.01765, -78.81122, which match the brief). Two searches and a few page reads turned up nothing else about a Mount Seneca lookout: no build date, builder, staffing or removal date. The Allegany State Park article's history section describes three park fire lookout towers (Summit, Tuscarora, Irvine) and does not mention a Mount Seneca tower. The article does list Mt. Seneca as the end of the Bear Caves trail, so the name appears there, but not as a tower. The platform may be an unrecorded or non-tower lookout, or the FFLA entry may be incomplete; neither is established. Elevation 2,106 ft (642 m) is from Peakery and is now recorded in facts. The Bear Caves trail is listed in the park article; whether the summit is open to the public or reachable by that trail is not stated in any source read, so access is unset. Brief check: kind platform and status gone match FFLA; no corrections proposed.
